hints: Focus on what each condition really means, a filled 4s means $4s^2$ and paired 3d means at least 6 electrons in 3d or a full $3d^{10}$.
Write the isolated gaseous atom configurations for iron ($Z=26$) and gallium ($Z=31$), both end in $4s^2$ with more than 5 electrons in 3d.
Remember copper is the famous exception with only one 4s electron, so check which two statements survive both tests together.
walkthrough:
**Translate the two conditions**

We need both at the same time. Filled 4s subshell means $4s^2$ (2 electrons). Paired in 3d means at least one 3d orbital holds 2 electrons.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{5 x 3d orbitals can hold max 10 electrons, pairing starts at the 6th electron}$$

**Test iron, statement 1**

Iron is $Z = 26$. Its isolated gaseous atom is $[Ar] 3d^6 4s^2$.

$$\text{Fe: } 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^6 4s^2$$
This has $4s^2$, so filled. $3d^6$ means five singly occupied plus one pair, so paired 3d is present. Statement 1 is true.

**Test gallium, statement 2**

Gallium is $Z = 31$. Its configuration is $[Ar] 3d^{10} 4s^2 4p^1$.

$$\text{Ga: } ... 3d^{10} 4s^2 4p^1$$
This has $4s^2$, so filled. $3d^{10}$ is completely filled, so all five 3d orbitals are paired. Statement 2 is true.

**Test copper, statement 3**

Copper is $Z = 29$ but it is anomalous as an isolated atom. It promotes one 4s electron to gain a full d subshell.

$$\text{Cu: } [Ar] 3d^{10} 4s^1 \text{ not } 3d^9 4s^2$$
It does have paired 3d electrons, but its 4s is half filled, not filled. So it fails one condition. Statement 3 is false.

**Combine the conclusion**

Only 1 and 2 satisfy both conditions together. That corresponds to the 1 and 2 only combination.

options.A: Incorrect. This option claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Iron and gallium are correct, but copper is $[Ar] 3d^{10} 4s^1$ with only one 4s electron, so it does not have a filled 4s subshell.
options.B: Correct. Iron ($3d^6 4s^2$) has a filled 4s and one paired 3d pair, and gallium ($3d^{10} 4s^2 4p^1$) has a filled 4s and fully paired 3d. Copper fails the filled 4s test, so only 1 and 2 are correct.
options.C: Incorrect. This option claims 2 and 3 only are correct. Gallium (2) is correct, but copper (3) is wrong because of its $4s^1$ configuration, and it wrongly leaves out iron (1) which fully satisfies both conditions.
options.D: Incorrect. This option claims 1 only is correct. Iron (1) is indeed correct, but gallium (2) is also correct with $3d^{10} 4s^2$, so limiting to 1 alone misses a valid element.
